Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Please help! Monstera Prop not going well?

Tl;Dr I tried to save my dying monstera by propagating the only healthy looking bits that were left. It's been in a jug of water with spagham moss, water gets changed regularly, it's been 3 weeks and I have no roots yet..

After a week or two of it not recovering, I decided I needed to do emergency surgery. I watched some YouTube videos on propagating monstera and I cut the "middle" section out of the plant, as that's where the "healthiest" looking leaves remained. I used a clean, fresh razor blade to make the cuts and did exactly as the video said... I have changed the water out every 3-4 days. The leaves still look unchanged, no better or worse, but there are no signs of new roots or new growth anywhere and the areas that were cut have just turned brown...

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely cause: stem rot, which is spreading from the cut ends and from the parent plant's base.** The dark, sunken, wet-looking lesions on the cuttings are at the cut ends and near the nodes, and the cuttings have no new roots after three weeks. A cutting without a node cannot root and will tend to rot instead. A cutting without a node cannot root; it will rot instead. Your photos also show the lesions creeping along the stem, not just at the cut. The root mass in the pot looks dark and thin, so the parent plant is likely rotting too. Dying roots are the usual reason a monstera declines, and stem rot is basically very advanced root rot.

**Quick checks:**
- **Stem base:** Press the stem at soil level. Firm tissue suggests the parent can be saved; soft, dark tissue that gives under light pressure means the crown is gone. Soft, dark, and wet when pressed means crown rot has set in, and repotting will not save the plant.
- **Roots:** Unpot and rinse. Healthy roots are firm and pale, while rotten roots are brown or black and pull apart easily.
- **Nodes:** Check each cutting for a node with firm, green tissue. If there isn't one, it likely won't recover.

**Fix:**
1. **Trim the cuttings** with a sterilized blade back to firm, pale green tissue, then let the cut dry for about an hour. Keep only pieces with a node.
2. **Change the setup.** A closed jug with wet moss holds too much moisture. Keeping the moss too wet will lead to stem rot, which will sabotage your propagation. Use clean water in a clear jar, keep the cut ends out of the water, and change the water every few days. Good airflow helps.
3. **Rescue the parent plant.** Cut back every brown, soft root to white tissue. Repot in a chunky aroid mix in a pot with a drainage hole, sized just a little larger than the roots. Water only when the top 2 to 3 inches are dry, and hold fertilizer until new growth appears.

If the parent's stem base is firm, it may recover. If it isn't, your cuttings are your best chance.
